title: School singing with Miss Clark and no instrument
summary: Elsie Clark taught songs by ear at school, and when a band instructor arrived his parents could not afford an instrument for him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Just say her name again, will you, Jay?

This was Elsie Clark. And she -- the way she would do, she would go to all the schools, but we only got that music maybe once every two or three weeks, you know. But I was always glad to see her come in and I never knew why,
but it seemed like it always felt good when Miss Clark would come in. They'd say, "Oh, Miss Clark will be here today," you know.
She would be teaching or just singing?
Would she be -- what would she have taught you? Would she have taught you the value of the notes or --
No, just singing, just orally, just singing, you know.

Because I think the piano that she had, it was just about gone, too, you know, but she could get by and she'd get her point across, you know, and so I never really had given music any thought but later on, after I got further along in school, I -- they had a band instructor -- they finally got a band instructor there and so they was trying to get parents to buy the instruments for their kids, you know.
